title: RunScores
description: A run bundle's scores.json: the researcher's judgements on the three measures section 3.5.7 names and does not define. Every field name here is data-management.md section 3's `scores.json` list verbatim -- scenarios/tests/ parses that list out of the protocol file and asserts the two key sets are equal, rather than a reviewer comparing them by eye (ADR-016's pattern). What this schema adds, and what data-management.md section 3 says it must add -- "the value range of each judged field is fixed by the M5 rubric, not here" -- is the range of each judged field. Those ranges are scenarios/groundtruth/rubric-v1.md's and ADR-037's; changing one after v1.0 is a hotfix ADR listing the affected runs.

run_id.description: RUN-<COND>-<SCN>-<INJ>-<SEED>, docs/07-glossary-and-ids.md. The bundle this judgement belongs to, carried inside the file as well as by its path, so a scores.json separated from its directory is still attributable.

rubric_version.description: Which revision of scenarios/groundtruth/rubric-v1.md produced these values. A judgement is only comparable to another judgement made under the same rubric, and the test-retest statistic M7 reports is meaningless across two.

passes.description: One entry per scoring pass. The re-score sample fraction, the delay before it and the agreement statistic are set at GATE and recorded in evaluation-protocol section 4 -- all three are literal placeholders there today, and none of them is restated here.

blind.description: Whether this pass was made through the blind view (scripts/blind_view.py). A bundle read directly is not blind: it carries `condition` in its manifest and its arm in its own directory name. The rubric states the residual leak the view cannot close rather than claiming none.

investigation_match.description: Ordinal 0-3 with anchored descriptors, judged against the scenario's ground-truth detection labels. Range fixed by rubric-v1.md section 1. Ordinal because the anchors are ordered and unequally spaced; it is never averaged across scenarios.

scope_correct.description: Binary, judged against the scenario's ground-truth blast_radius. Binary because section 3.5.7 calls it a "judgement" rather than a score, and a scale would invent gradations the source does not have.

incorrect_or_harmful_action_count.description: Non-negative integer, counted under rubric-v1.md section 3's explicit rule joined to guardian_audit.jsonl. A count with no counting rule is an impression with a number on it, which is exactly what a test-retest statistic would then be measuring.
